property_summary: After any sequence of calls to Put, the sum of balances of all holders in the reference contract never exceeds the total Ether sent into the contract; the mutant can overflow a balance, causing total balances to exceed the contract's Ether balance.

For any Holder, the balance never exceeds the maximum possible accumulated Put amount for that address due to overflow; the mutant allows overflow causing balance to wrap around, violating the invariant that balance is monotonic with respect to total Put calls.
For any address, its Acc balance must equal the sum of all Ether sent via Put to that address; the mutant allows silent overflow so the balance can be less than the total sent (or even zero).

After any call to Put, the caller's balance in the reference contract remains strictly greater than their previous balance (monotonic increase) because overflow is prevented; the mutant allows overflow, so a sufficiently large msg.value can cause the balance to wrap around and be smaller than before.

For any single Put call, the caller's resulting balance equals their previous balance plus msg.value; the mutant allows overflow so for a large enough msg.value the balance wraps and fails this equality.
After a call to Put, the unlockTime recorded for msg.sender must be >= block.timestamp; the bug uses the raw _unlockTime which can be in the past, violating this invariant.
After a call to Put, the unlockTime for the caller must never be less than the block.timestamp of the next block; the buggy version allows it to be in the past by using the raw _unlockTime.

For every Put call, the recorded unlockTime must not be less than the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the bug accepts a past _unlockTime, making the recorded unlockTime potentially less than the call's block.timestamp.
After a Put, the caller's unlock time is at least the current block timestamp; the bug allows it to be earlier.

After a Put call, the caller's unlockTime must never be strictly less than the block.timestamp that existed at the start of the Put call; the bug accepts a past _unlockTime, so it can set unlockTime to a value that was already in the past relative to the call's block.timestamp, violating this invariant.

After any call to Put, the unlockTime stored in Acc for msg.sender must equal the greater of the passed _unlockTime and block.timestamp, but the mutant always sets it to block.timestamp, violating this invariant when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any call to Put with an _unlockTime greater than block.timestamp, the stored unlockTime must equal _unlockTime; the mutant always stores block.timestamp, so it differs whenever _unlockTime > block.timestamp.
After any call to Put, the stored unlockTime must be at least the passed _unlockTime; the mutant stores block.timestamp instead, violating this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After any call to Put, the stored unlockTime must equal the maximum of the passed _unlockTime and block.timestamp; the mutant always stores block.timestamp, violating this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After any call to Put from any address, the account's unlockTime in Acc must be at least block.timestamp, which the reference satisfies and the mutant also satisfies (both set it to >= block.timestamp), so the difference is in the exact value; the mutant changes the exact value to block.timestamp regardless of input, so the invariant that the stored unlockTime equals the maximum of the passed _unlockTime and block.timestamp is the universal rule that the reference holds and the bug breaks when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.
After calling Put, the last History entry's Data must equal 'Put'. The bug writes 'Put2' instead.
After calling Put, the message stored in LogFile's LastMsg must have Data equal to 'Put'. The bug writes 'Put2' instead, breaking this invariant.
After any call to Put, the Data field of the last message logged by LogFile must be 'Put'; the mutant writes 'Put2' and violates this.

After any call to Put through C, querying C's Acc mapping for the caller should never revert or behave inconsistently due to LogFile's LastMsg Data; the bug writes 'Put2' which does not interfere with the Acc state, but the invariant checks that the operation completes without reverting and leaves Acc[caller].balance consistent with the sent value.
After any successful Put call, the Data field of the last message in LogFile's History must equal the string 'Put'; the mutant writes 'Put2', violating this invariant.
After any Put call, the Log contract's History array length must increase by exactly 1; the buggy version omits the log, so the length does not increase.
After a successful Put, the last message stored in the Log contract must have the sender equal to the caller; the buggy version omits the log, so the last sender will not update.
After any Put call, the Log contract's History array length must increase by exactly 1; the buggy version omits the log, so the length does not increase.

After any call to Put(some unlockTime), the Acc mapping's balance for the caller is strictly greater than before the call; the buggy version satisfies this too, so the difference must be observed through the Log contract, but the only public Log surface is via its external AddMessage or the public History array. The correct Put emits Put data to Log via AddMessage, so a successful Put must eventually be reflected in the Log's History. However, the earlier tried rules around History length increase were rejected. Since no other public state of C changes, the only invariant difference is that in the correct contract a successful Put call causes a new Log message to be appended with the caller's address and value; the buggy contract does not append any message. Thus, the rule is: for any caller and any positive value, after calling Put, the last message in Log.History has the caller as Sender and the value as Val; the buggy version violates this because it never updates the Log.

For any caller and any value, after calling Put, the Log contract's LastMsg.Sender equals the caller and LastMsg.Val equals the sent value; the buggy version omits the log, so these fields do not update to the caller's values.

property_summary: After a Collect that does not revert, the contract's ETH balance must be strictly less than twice the deposit minus the collected amount.
After any valid Collect operation that subtracts _am from balance, the balance must decrease; the mutant adds _am instead and increases balance when Collect is executed.

After a Collect operation that succeeds, the contract's balance of the caller must not exceed the caller's balance before the Collect plus any Ether sent with the call (i.e., balance must decrease or stay the same after a collect, never increase); the mutant adds _am to balance instead of subtracting it, causing an increase.

After a successful Collect, the caller's Acc balance must be less than or equal to its balance before the call minus the collected amount; the mutant adds instead of subtracting, so the balance strictly increases.

For any admissible Collect call that succeeds, the caller's Acc balance after the call must be strictly less than or equal to its balance before the call; the mutant adds _am instead of subtracting, so the balance strictly increases when _am > 0.
After a successful Collect that sends ETH, the caller's balance must equal the previous balance minus the collected amount; the bug turns subtraction into addition, so balance increases instead.

property_summary: Collect reverts unless the account balance meets both the minimum sum and the requested amount simultaneously (the unlock time cannot override these checks).

After a deposit with a future unlock time, a collection attempt should not reduce the balance when block.timestamp is not past unlock time, but the mutant's OR logic allows it to succeed.

For any account with enough balance but whose unlockTime is in the future, calling Collect must never decrease that account's balance; the mutant's OR condition lets it succeed and decrease the balance prematurely.
After a deposit with unlockTime in the future, calling Collect must revert when block.timestamp <= unlockTime, but the mutant's OR condition allows successful early withdrawal.

For any caller, after a successful Collect operation (no revert), the caller's balance in Acc must only decrease if block.timestamp exceeds the caller's unlockTime; the mutant's OR condition allows balance decrease even when block.timestamp <= unlockTime.
